claims.text: Incorporating graphene nanoplatelets into a silicon nitride matrix yields a high-temperature self-lubricating composite.
The graphene–silicon nitride composite balances superior mechanical strength with reduced friction across a wide temperature range.
Controlled dispersion and optimized sintering can produce a uniform graphene-nanoplatelet/silicon-nitride composite.
Sliding activates graphene nanoplatelets to form a continuous lubricious film between contacting surfaces.
Graphene's layered structure provides low-shear interfaces that reduce friction.
The silicon nitride matrix maintains mechanical integrity and load-bearing capacity in the composite.
The combination of low-shear graphene interfaces and a robust silicon nitride matrix enables stable tribological performance across a wide temperature range.
Compared with pure silicon nitride, the graphene-reinforced composite will have a lower coefficient of friction at low and high temperatures.
Compared with pure silicon nitride, the graphene-reinforced composite will have reduced wear rates at low and high temperatures.
Graphene reinforcement will provide friction and wear reductions without a significant loss of mechanical strength.
Pure silicon nitride has high mechanical strength.
Pure silicon nitride has limited self-lubricating properties, particularly under varying temperatures.
Excessive graphene content may reduce mechanical strength because of interfacial weaknesses.
Optimal graphene dispersion and volume fraction are critical to balancing lubrication and mechanical strength.
The long-term high-temperature oxidation stability of the graphene-containing composite is uncertain.
